'''Detlef Lohse''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2025/05/new-fellows/ |access-date=2025-05-20 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref> (born 15 September 1963 in [[Hamburg]]) is a German physicist (fluid dynamicist) and professor in the [[University of Twente]]'s Department of [[fluid mechanics|Physics of Fluids]] in the [[Netherlands]].<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=http://pof.tnw.utwente.nl/ |title=Physics of Fluids – Home |publisher=pof.tnw.utwente.nl |date= |access-date=15 November 2018}}</ref>

==Biography==
Lohse studied at the [[University of Kiel]] and [[University of Bonn]], graduating in [[Bonn]] in 1989 with a degree in [[Physics]], and completed his [[PhD]] at the [[University of Marburg]] in 1992 with Professor Siegfried Grossmann on "Fully developed turbulence," receiving his doctorate summa cum laude (with distinction).<ref name="cv-2025">{{cite web|url=https://pof.tnw.utwente.nl/media/files/downloads/cv/Detlef%20Lohse%20CV%20January%202025.pdf|title=Detlef Lohse: Curriculum Vitae|publisher=pof.tnw.utwente.nl|date=August 2024|access-date=26 March 2025}}</ref> He served as a postdoctoral research fellow at the [[University of Chicago]] with [[Leo Kadanoff]] from 1993 to 1995, which he later described as a formative experience in his scientific career.<ref name="transcript">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yvCF65iE8Mw|title=Detlef Lohse: Living Histories talk transcript|publisher=YouTube|access-date=26 March 2025}}</ref> In 1997 he got his [[Habilitation]] in theoretical physics at the University of Marburg on the subject of [[Sonoluminescence]].  He joined [[University of Twente]] in 1998 where he leads the Physics of Fluids department.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://pof.tnw.utwente.nl/media/files/downloads/cv/Detlef%20Lohse%20CV%20January%202019.pdf |title=Detlef Lohse: Curriculum Vitae |publisher=Pof.tnw.utwente.nl |date=1 January 2019 |access-date=11 March 2020}}</ref> 

Lohse has been an external member of the [[Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization]] in [[Göttingen|Göttingen, Germany]] since 2015. Since 2016, he is a founding member of the [https://www.utwente.nl/en/max-planck-center/#:~:text=The%20center%20is%20composed%20by,of%20Albert%20van%20den%20Berg. Max Planck Center for Complex Fluid Dynamics] at [[University of Twente]].<ref name="cv-2025"></ref>

He is married with two children.<ref name="cv-2025" />

==Scientific work and recognition==
Lohse's research spans a wide range of topics in fluid dynamics. His present work includes [[turbulence]] and two-phase flows, thermal convection, granular flow, micro- and nanofluidics, and the biomedical application of [[Liquid bubble|bubbles]].<ref name="cv-2025" />

Lohse's work spans diverse areas of fluid dynamics. His research on turbulence and two-phase flows includes studies of fully developed turbulence, particularly thermally driven turbulence ([[Rayleigh–Bénard convection]]) and [[Taylor–Couette flow]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ahlers |first1=Guenter |last2=Grossmann |first2=Siegfried |last3=Lohse |first3=Detlef |date=2009-04-22 |title=Heat transfer and large scale dynamics in turbulent Rayleigh-B\'enard convection |url=https://journals.aps.org/rmp/abstract/10.1103/RevModPhys.81.503 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=81 |issue=2 |pages=503–537 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.81.503|arxiv=0811.0471 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lohse |first1=Detlef |last2=Shishkina |first2=Olga |date=2024-08-06 |title=Ultimate Rayleigh-B\'enard turbulence |url=https://journals.aps.org/rmp/abstract/10.1103/RevModPhys.96.035001 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=96 |issue=3 |article-number=035001 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.96.035001|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His groundbreaking work on bubble dynamics and sonoluminescence (the emission of light from acoustically driven bubbles) helped solve a longstanding scientific puzzle by explaining the phenomenon through bubble shape stability, diffusive stability, chemical stability, and energy focusing.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Brenner |first1=Michael P. |last2=Hilgenfeldt |first2=Sascha |last3=Lohse |first3=Detlef |date=2002-05-13 |title=Single-bubble sonoluminescence |url=https://journals.aps.org/rmp/abstract/10.1103/RevModPhys.74.425 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=74 |issue=2 |pages=425–484 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.74.425}}</ref> In the field of micro- and nanofluidics, he investigates fluid behavior at microscopic and nanoscopic scales.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Lohse |first1=Detlef |last2=Zhang |first2=Xuehua|author2-link=Xuehua Zhang |date=2015-08-31 |title=Surface nanobubbles and nanodroplets |url=https://journals.aps.org/rmp/abstract/10.1103/RevModPhys.87.981 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=87 |issue=3 |pages=981–1035 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.87.981}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lohse |first1=Detlef |last2=Zhang |first2=Xuehua |author2-link=Xuehua Zhang|title=Physicochemical hydrodynamics of droplets out of equilibrium |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s42254-020-0199-z |journal=Nature Reviews Physics |date=2020 |language=en |volume=2 |issue=8 |pages=426–443 |doi=10.1038/s42254-020-0199-z |issn=2522-5820}}</ref> His research on inkjet printing explores the fluid dynamics challenges in printing technologies.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ahlers |first1=Guenter |last2=Grossmann |first2=Siegfried |last3=Lohse |first3=Detlef |date=2009-04-22 |title=Heat transfer and large scale dynamics in turbulent Rayleigh-B\'enard convection |url=https://journals.aps.org/rmp/abstract/10.1103/RevModPhys.81.503 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=81 |issue=2 |pages=503–537 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.81.503|arxiv=0811.0471 }}</ref> Lohse has conducted pioneering work on surface nanobubbles and nanodroplets, studying the stability and properties of nanoscopic bubbles on surfaces.<ref name=":0" /> His investigations into granular flows address the complex behaviors of granular materials. Additionally, he researches biomedical applications of bubbles, examining their use in medical diagnostics and treatments. His research philosophy emphasizes cross-fertilization between different areas of fluid dynamics, allowing insights from one field to inform solutions in others.<ref name="transcript" />

His research combines experiment, theory, and numerical simulation, addressing both fundamental science and problems with practical applications. As Lohse states in his approach to science: "There is no difference between fundamental and applied research. There is only a difference between good research and bad research."<ref name="transcript" /> His work has significance for climate science, energy transition, environmental issues, health, high technology, and fundamental fluid mechanics.<ref name="transcript" />

One of his most notable contributions was solving the puzzle of single-bubble sonoluminescence, which has applications in ultrasound diagnostics, inkjet printing, underwater acoustics, cavitation, and marine geophysical surveys.<ref name="transcript" /> Lohse has described his approach to scientific problems as being like solving puzzles, collecting pieces through reading, calculation, experimentation, and numerical simulations until they form a complete picture.<ref name="transcript" />

He has published over 773 refereed publications<ref name="cv-2025" /> with over 178 of them in the ''[[Journal of Fluid Mechanics]]'', making him the largest contributor to that journal. His work has been cited approximately 54,000 times (according to Google Scholar) with an h-index of 122.<ref name="cv-2025" />

Professor Lohse was a recipient of the 2019 [[Max Planck Medal]], 2018 [[Balzan Prize]], 2017 [[Fluid Dynamics Prize]], 2012 [[Batchelor Prize]], 2005 [[Spinoza Prize]] for his work on [[turbulence]], [[thermal convection]], [[multiphase flow]], [[microfluidics]], [[sonoluminescence]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nwo.nl/nwohome.nsf/pages/NWOP_6CYJ9W_Eng |title=NWO – NWO/Spinoza prize to cancer research, cognitive sciences, physics and mathematics |publisher=Nwo.nl |access-date=8 December 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101024002729/http://www.nwo.nl/nwohome.nsf/pages/NWOP_6CYJ9W_Eng |archive-date=24 October 2010 }}</ref> and was awarded with a [[State decoration|knighthood]] in the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.utwente.nl/en/news/2010/3/116727/royal-honor-for-professor-lohse |title=Royal honor for professor Lohse |publisher=Utwente.nl |date=30 March 2010 |access-date=11 March 2020 }}</ref>

Additional major honors include three [[European Research Council]] (ERC) Advanced Grants (2010, 2017, 2023), membership in the National Academy of Engineering of the United States (elected 2017), the Simon-Stevin-Meesterschap Prize (2009), and the AkzoNobel Science Award (2012).<ref name="cv-2025" />

His work has been recognized with numerous "Gallery of Fluid Motion" awards at the American Physical Society Division of Fluid Dynamics meetings, including several Milton van Dyke Prizes for outstanding visual presentations of flow phenomena.<ref name="cv-2025" />

He is also a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 2005,<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/leden/6710 |title=Detlef Lohse |language=Dutch |publisher=[[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] |date= |access-date=30 June 2015 |archive-date=3 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200603164259/https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/leden/6710 }}</ref> a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] since 2017, a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], a member of the German Academy of Sciences "Leopoldina" (elected 2002), a Fellow of the Institute of Physics (elected 2004), a member of the Netherlands Academy of Technology and Innovation (elected 2017),<ref name="cv-2025" /> and a Foreign Member of the [[Fellow of the Royal Society|Royal Society]] (elected 2025).<ref name=":2" />

== Scientific citizenship ==

Lohse has made substantial contributions to the scientific community through leadership roles, editorial service, conference organization, and mentorship.

=== Leadership in scientific organizations ===
In professional societies, Lohse has served in numerous leadership positions:
* Vice-Chair, Chair-elect, Chair, and Past-Chair of the American Physical Society's Division of Fluid Dynamics (DFD) Executive Board (2020-2023)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Chairman of the IUTAM Fluid Mechanics Symposia Panel (2016-2024)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Elected Member of the General Assembly of IUTAM (2018-2024)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Elected Member of the IUTAM Bureau (2020-2024)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Elected Member of the Euromech Council (2004-2010)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Chairman of the Advisory Board for the Lorentz Center in Leiden (2015-2023)<ref name="cv-2025"/>

In Dutch scientific administration, he has served as:
* Member of the Board of FOM (2003-2014) and of the Executive Board of FOM (2007-2016)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Vice-Chair of FOM (2012-2016) and Vice-Chair of the NWO Exact Sciences "Table for Physics" (2018-2021)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Chairman of the FOM group on Fluid Dynamics (2002-2008)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Member of the KNAW Domeinjury for the selection of new KNAW members (2012-2018)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Member of the Excellence Commission and of the Committee of Experts for the Excellence Strategy of the German Science Foundation (DFG) (2016-2024)<ref name="cv-2025"/>

=== Editorial contributions ===
Lohse has served on numerous editorial boards:
* Associate Editor and Member of the Editorial Board of Journal of Fluid Mechanics (2007-present)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Editor of Science Advances (2019-2021)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Member of the Editorial Board of Annual Reviews of Fluid Mechanics (2008, 2014, 2016-2020)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Editor and Member of the Editorial Board of Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment (JSTAT) (2003-present)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Previously served on editorial boards for Physica D (2003-2015), Nonlinearity (2002-2015), Physical Review E (2003-2008), Journal of Turbulence (2003-2017), and European Physical Journal B (2004-2007)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Occasional Editor for the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (PNAS) (2015-present)<ref name="cv-2025"/>

=== Conference organization ===
Lohse has organized numerous scientific conferences, workshops, and summer schools:
* Co-Organizer of the Conference "Droplets 2015" in Twente (220 participants)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Co-Organizer of the Conference "Flow14" in Twente (450 participants)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Co-Organizer of the IUTAM Colloquium on "Dispersed multiphase flow" in Mexico (2015)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Organization of Euromech colloquia and Lorentz Center workshops on "Hydrodynamics of bubbly flows," "Micro- and nanofluidics," and "Contact-line instabilities"<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Organizer of two KNAW Webinars on Covid-19 spreading by aerosols (2020 and 2021)<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Initiator and Director of the Max-Planck Center "Complex Fluid Dynamics" between Twente and the Max-Planck Institutes in Göttingen and Mainz (2016-2028)<ref name="cv-2025"/>

=== Mentorship and education ===
A significant aspect of Lohse's career has been mentoring the next generation of scientists:
* His group has educated more than 120 PhD students, with approximately 30 currently working on their theses <ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics of Fluids - People - PhDs |url=https://pof.tnw.utwente.nl/people/phd |access-date=2025-03-26 |website=pof.tnw.utwente.nl}}</ref>
* About 75 of his former PhD students and postdocs now hold professorships worldwide<ref name="cv-2025"/><ref name="transcript"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics of Fluids - People - Alumni |url=https://pof.tnw.utwente.nl/people/alumni/alumniprofs |access-date=2025-03-26 |website=pof.tnw.utwente.nl}}</ref>
* Several startup companies have emerged from his Physics of Fluids Department, including ACFD Consultancy, Tide Microfluidics, Bubclean, and Iamfluidics<ref name="cv-2025"/>
* Multiple students under his supervision have won national and international prizes for their theses, including the ERCOFTAC da Vinci Award, FOM Prize, Charles Hoogendoorn Award (H. Gelderblom, S. Huisman, V. Sanjay, J. Meijer),<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-26 |title=Hoogendoorn KIVI Award |url=https://www.tudelft.nl/jmburgerscentrum/awards/hoogendoorn-kivi-award |access-date=2025-03-26}}</ref> and Shell-Master-Thesis Prize in Physics<ref name="cv-2025"/>

Lohse has demonstrated his commitment to science education through teaching activities including course lectures on "Physics of Fluids," "Dynamics," and "Advanced Fluid Mechanics," as well as special lectures on topics such as turbulence, granular flow, and stochastic processes.<ref name="cv-2025"/>
